title: Does Consumer Protection Enhance Disclosure Credibility in Reward Crowdfunding?

scopes.description: Complete author-documented workflow including R text preparation, SAS dataset construction, and Stata analyses.

requirements.description: Kickstarter campaign-tab raw data for the author scrape; R text analysis requires Link/Text/RiskAndChallenges and SAS cleaning requires campaign dates, location, funding, status, category, and backer fields. Author reports projects launched 2009–2017, scraped July–September 2017.

routes.description: Author-named Web Robots snapshots are a candidate supplement, but page-level monthly snapshots do not establish the campaign schema, full 2009–2017 coverage, or equivalence to the authors’ seeded scrape.
routes.expected_period: Author scrape reports 2009–2017 campaign launches and July–September 2017 compilation. SAS also aggregates state pledging by beg_year-1; if the earliest analysis year is 2009, 2008 campaign history may be needed. Exact scope/filter bounds and missing-lag treatment require confirmation.

requirements.description: Kickstarter creator-tab raw data joined by Link; SAS derives creator state/country, foreign status, Facebook count, biography lengths, projects backed/created, last login, and author/name fields.

routes.description: Same author-named snapshot collection is only a candidate; creator-tab field names and coverage are not verified.
routes.expected_period: Creator profiles for campaign projects in the author’s 2009–2017 study coverage; precise snapshot date and coverage unresolved.

routes.description: Candidate historical project snapshots; the community-tab schema and author scrape coverage are not verified.
routes.expected_period: Project coverage corresponding to the 2009–2017 campaign sample; exact tab history unresolved.

requirements.description: Kickstarter comments-tab raw data joined by Link; R fraud analysis needs the full comment Transcript and SAS uses comment and reply counts/lengths.

routes.description: Candidate historical project snapshots; comments/transcripts, comment dates, coverage, and author equivalence are not established by the listing.
routes.expected_period: Comments available by the authors’ July–September 2017 collection for projects launched 2009–2017; exact post-project coverage unresolved.

routes.description: Candidate project snapshots; the updates-tab schema and complete coverage are not verified.

requirements.description: NORC General Social Survey cumulative cross-sectional file; SAS uses id, year, region, trust, comphome, and courts to derive region-year measures matched to project start years.

routes.description: NORC offers a cumulative SAS file; the current release is 1972–2024, while the author input is gss7216_r1a (through 2016). Confirm required variables and compatible vintage/semantics before substitution.
routes.expected_period: Author file gss7216_r1a is 1972–2016; project measures select earlier/equal survey years, with nearest-year handling for computer-at-home.

requirements.description: Daily currency exchange rates to USD from Datastream; SAS needs date, currency, and exchange_rate for non-USD project goal currencies.

routes.expected_period: Calendar years 1998–2017 in the author’s February 2019 data vintage; project-year matching uses beg_year.

issues.description: The R fraud branch loads camdate.RData containing Link/beg_date/end_date, but neither supplied R program produces it. SAS cleaning does derive beg_date/end_date from CAM fundingperiod and endedon fields, but no SAS-to-R export or interleaving is specified.

The R preparation program saves reduced CAMNEW/CRENEW/COMNEW/COTNEW/UPDNEW RData, while SAS reads separate raw_data SAS tables. CAMNEW drops Text/RiskAndChallenges that SAS cleaning uses; COTNEW drops Transcript required by R fraud. The datasheet names Stat/Transfer generically but does not map original versus reduced inputs, output names/paths, column preservation, or the exact metric-to-SAS table contracts.

SAS expects raw_data.city_state_nomatch_nomatch_d after programmatic matching. The source comments say unmatched rows are exported for manual matching, but the crosswalk file, field schema, matching decisions, and return/import procedure are not supplied.

The official Census adjacency file has four named fields, while SAS reads a separate three-field C1/C2/C3 table and treats C3 as border_id. The derivation, state-name mapping, and border_id semantics are not supplied.

The supplied R, SAS, and Stata code use hard-coded [redacted-path-0aa1c7d5614f] paths, while the documented host batch workflow supports relative or [redacted-path-c86a2477fb8b] paths. A coordinated host-visible project tree must preserve the existing R raw_data/data, SAS raw_data/data, and Stata data/ado/log/output roles.

SAS creates a prior-calendar-year state pledge ratio from beg_year-1 and explicitly sets a missing resulting ratio to zero. The datasheet reports campaign coverage of 2009–2017, but the exact analysis-sample lower bound and available pre-sample campaign history cannot be quantified without the raw input. Preserve the source zero fill and do not infer a sample defect from the identifier count or R batch bound.

The datasheet documents SAS dset_final.sas7bdat followed by Stat/Transfer to the Stata input dset_final.dta.

actions.description: Obtain the five required Kickstarter raw tabs and preserve the author’s project-link coverage and 2017 collection window. The Web Robots archive is a candidate supplement only until it matches the author fields and full historical/tab coverage.

If using the documented Web Robots material, select a specific historical snapshot only after matching the required fields in each tab and checking project launches across the reported 2009–2017 period; retain the author scrape and Web Robots component provenance separately.
Stage the campaign, creator, community, comments, and updates sources under the selected project raw-data tree; preserve Link values and the full COT Transcript needed for fraud text analysis.

Check Link-key completeness and the comments transcript/date coverage before any metric generation; do not infer coverage from a single row count.

Keep the source text unchanged and record the row count/hash used for the conversion; do not treat this list as a substitute for campaign, creator, community, comments, or updates data.

Treat SAS data.cam as a candidate only after confirming the cleaned dates can be extracted into the Link/date shape consumed by R. A separately prepared compatible date table is also sufficient; author confirmation is optional when the field and coverage mapping is demonstrated.

Verify the fraud branch classifies comments relative to project end dates after a future authorized run.

actions.description: Document the raw campaign coverage needed for SAS’s prior-calendar-year state aggregation while preserving its explicit missing-to-zero rule.

Preserve the SAS merge on beg_year-1 and the explicit assignment of zero when the merged ratio is missing; do not fabricate earlier observations or infer a defect from the listed sample identifiers.

Keep the authored zero fill unchanged and compare the resulting nonmissing aggregate coverage in a future authorized run.

actions.description: Obtain a compatible cumulative GSS SAS source and retain the year-selection behavior in the author’s SAS code.

Record the selected release/version; ensure the history includes the survey years needed for the project’s earlier/equal-year matches and the nearest-year computer-at-home calculation.

Confirm selected trust/courts observations are no later than project begin years and computer-at-home matching follows the authored nearest-year rule.

Verify the SAS join selects the most recent rate dated zero to ten days before beg_date and leaves USD projects unchanged.

Prepare the state plus v1998–v2017 wide table expected by SAS without changing the unit or revising historical values silently.

Confirm SAS transpose yields the expected state-year keys and project-year matches.

Confirm the measure sums incoming newly filed, reopened, and reactivated cases across civil, domestic relations, criminal, juvenile, and traffic cases and retains the author’s per-capita denominator.

Confirm the SAS merge uses the closest prior-or-equal survey year and preserves missing values as authored.

Return the table under the expected SAS libref and filename with the input fields needed by the append.

Record remaining unmatched locations and confirm the SAS append preserves all source rows.

actions.description: Resolve how the official Census adjacency product becomes the author’s three-field border table.

Confirm the meaning and construction of C1, C2, and C3/border_id, including county/state name mapping; do not infer a border indicator from the four raw Census fields without the author’s rule.

Check county matches before and after the border join and preserve all campaign rows.

Confirm the SAS join selects the nearest report within 365 days and reproduces the separate state/metro aggregates without silently changing the bank population.

After a separately authorized future run, verify SAS/Stata outputs, key variables and Link joins, and Stata tables/logs; this proposal is not execution evidence.

Confirm each required SAS table has the expected Link key and no source fields needed for later stages were removed.

review_notes: Checkpoint: the datasheet names four stages—R project-file preparation/text analysis, Stat/Transfer conversion into SAS, three SAS macros that clean/merge/build dset_final.sas7bdat, then Stat/Transfer conversion to dset_final.dta and the Stata driver. The assessed full-pipeline entry points are the two supplied R programs, the supplied SAS program, and the supplied Stata do-file.

The R fraud section additionally consumes camdate.RData and sample.RData with no producer found among the supplied code. Its derived fraud.RData has no documented automatic conversion to the SAS raw_data.fraud table. SAS also consumes distinct SAS files for every R-derived metric; actual conversion, paths, and column mapping remain to be reconciled.

The identifier TXT is a 255,018-line final-sample link list, while the R program processes CAM in batches through row 332,364. The identifier file is not the raw campaign/comments/creator/community/updates inputs or the final analysis dataset; the count difference alone does not show a sample error.

The appendix describes additional empirical analyses (FTC complaints/backer-comment aggregates, project-size partitions, additional robustness, and treatment-effect stability) without corresponding programs in this package. Keep these as context; assess all branches actually supplied in the two R files, SAS program, and Stata main-analysis driver.
Source and package contents have not been executed or deserialized. Continue local resource, software, route, path, and all-97 dependency review before finalization.

Coverage note: all 97 frozen dependency IDs are mapped below. D0001–D0007 are original RData inputs; D0010–D0018 are separate SAS raw inputs. Do not assume the R readfiles outputs alone are valid SAS inputs: CAMNEW drops Text/RiskAndChallenges that SAS uses, while COTNEW drops Transcript used by R fraud.

Temporal coverage note: SAS uses GSS and court observations from years less than or equal to project begin year (nearest prior year for several series), uses a 0–10 day pre-begin FX match, uses bank reports within 365 days before or after project begin, and uses a prior-calendar-year state pledge aggregate. The broad campaign description says 2009–2017, but exact analysis filters/history bounds are unresolved; 2008 may be needed for the earliest prior-year state aggregate. The source’s R batch endpoint 332,364 and the identifier text’s 255,018 lines do not establish a sample defect.

Input interpretation note: the NCLC UDAP state treatment coding is embedded in the supplied SAS source; no separate NCLC table is read by these programs. Embedded legalese/novel dictionaries are code literals, not missing external model artifacts. The supplied appendix has additional analyses without matching code; they remain contextual because the selected scope is the provided R/SAS/Stata workflow.
